utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. If I could remind you once again, Mr. Hvalkof, of the affirmation you took at the beginning of your evidence. Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Rodic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hvalkof. I will continue with my questions. Would you please look at tab 9. This is the last page of the documentation entitled "Reasons for Evacuating the Monitoring Mission from Dubrovnik." Under item 2 can you explain further what it says here: "Both sides are constantly violating the cease-fire."

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That was apparently the opinion of the people who wrote this, that that was happening. I didn't read -- I didn't write it. But they're saying so. And if you want me to interpret that, it meant of course when -- as it has been mentioned by the Croats that when there was fighting going on or shelling or what have you, there was fire from both sides, yes. So the people who were defending themselves, the Croats, they would fire back, as they have also mentioned in messages when they felt they were attacked in their way. I'm not saying that that was happening. But when they claimed they were attacked, they would use fire. So the Croats were firing also during this conflict, yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please respond more briefly to my questions and focus on what I ask. It's quite unnecessary to tell me about the Croats returning fire, because I assume that returning fire should not count as a violation of a cease-fire. Do you understand the violation of a cease-fire to imply that somebody started the firing, opened fire first? Do I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any firing from any side, whether it's a cease-fire, is a break -- a breach of the cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have an opportunity to see the reports of your monitors in which they say that the Croats violated the cease-fire, the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When firing was going on and it was reported fire from both sides, and that was reported normally daily when it -- when it happened to our ops office. And it was registered there that there was fire in the area from both sides when it happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you keep saying "both sides," and expanding your reply? I'm asking you specifically about the Croatian side. Could you please be precise and tell me whether you received any such reports; if you did, how many there were, if you can remember. Would you just reply briefly to my question, please.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, reports were received; I can't remember the number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. There is also item 2 here in which it says that the ECMM monitors have the impression that they are now among enemies and that they can use this unscrupulously as a shield for their needs. My question is: Did at any time the monitors find themselves on positions of the other side, that is, at JNA positions, or were they always in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not always in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether a monitor spent the night on the other side on one occasion, and if he did can you tell me who, when, and where?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In item 4 it says that Dubrovnik is exposed to fire from land and sea and that the island of Lokrum, the Belvedere Hotel and all the suburbs have been targeted. Have you heard that there were Croatian military positions there?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at tab number 10. Yesterday in answer to my question on page 13 at 945, as to whether, according to the memorandum, all paramilitary and irregular units had to be disarmed and disbanded, including the reserve forces of the Croatian National Guard, the ZNG, and you replied that you did not remember the details of that document. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at the first two sentences in item 2 of this letter in tab 10. In the second sentence of the letter signed by you, you say: "I protest because this is completely contrary to Article 4 of the memorandum of understanding of the 1st of September, 1991."

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this means that you did read the memorandum?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I did know the details at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This detail in connection with the paramilitary units in Article 1 of the memorandum, have you forgotten it?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I have forgotten the details of the memorandum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wasn't this detail regulated in Article 1, the main reason why the memorandum was signed in the first place?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have answered that once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to ask you whether you have a selective memory in connection with problems concerning the Croatian side and the paramilitary units there.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can answer that I do my best to remember and the papers I have got to support me from 13, 14 years ago is a help to me. And I know what I wrote at that time - I said that yesterday - that was correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please now look at tab 11. On the 9th of November, you addressed the Main Staff of the JNA in Split. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And item 1 says you are referring to your previous protest, which you addressed to General Strugar. That's what we saw in tab 10 right now. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me to whom you addressed this protest from tab 10, the one referring to General Strugar. Did you send it to Split also?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We also passed a message, the same, to Split to be sure that it was passed through -- to be absolutely sure that everybody was informed. Because we were not always sure that our means of communication was working the best way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you send this to Dubrovnik or to Boka?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had already sent -- and this was, to the best of my knowledge, sort of making sure that the message was passed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "Split," does this refer to the military naval district? You addressed your letter to them?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. To Major General Mladenic and his staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item 2 of this letter says that you were informed by your people in Dubrovnik that there is fighting in the immediate vicinity of the Hotel Argentina. Can you tell me more about this? What does it mean when you say that there is fighting in the immediate vicinity of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were impacts of smaller arms. And if I remember in one of the earlier tabs, there are -- people are mentioning they cannot move a foot outside the door, the impacts are close to the hotel, and there is an exchange of fire right around in the area of the hotel. There are details in other of my papers about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this then mean that the Croatian forces were firing from near the Hotel Argentina, in view of the fact that the JNA never actually came close to the hotel. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm that there was fire on the hotel. Where the Croatian soldiers were positioned, I'm not aware of. They were not in the hotel or just outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 9th of November, were you in Hotel Argentina?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How then can you say this, because not even your monitors say this in the report they sent you?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge I asked them about the situation and also about -- if there were armed forces in the hotel. And to the very best of my knowledge, they also answered there were not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on. Tab 12, if you could please look at it. Can you read the last passage of this message.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last page?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, on the first page, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's my old handwriting again. Okay. "We've just now protested to the crisis committee" -- or it says "have just at 1315 protested to the crisis committee. It is impossible to get in contact with" -- and I -- I believe I have written here "it is impossible to get in contact with Strugar," and that is not very polite. It should of course be General Strugar, "and his second in command."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was the protest addressed by the monitor to the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because when anybody is firing for whatever reason when there is a cease-fire, you protest to the ones who are firing. Apparently the Croatians had also -- were firing, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please open tab 13. Is it correct that you are again addressing General Mladenic in Split on the 10th of November?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this mean that you were having problems in communicating with Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This means that you were also having problems in communicating with Boka. In your view, were Generals Mladenic and Strugar part of the same military formation?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but they had, to the best of my knowledge, communications, as I mentioned yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please now turn to tab 15. When you say to the best of your recollection Mladenic and Strugar, the two generals, had mutual contacts, do you remember that Mladenic was better able to contact Admiral Jokic because both of them were in the navy and Jokic's unit was part of the military and naval district of Split?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about the relations between these units as such in the organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know what units comprised the military naval district in Split?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know what the 9th VPS in Boka was?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never got these information -- these abbreviations. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me assist you. This is the 9th Military Naval Sector. Do you know what the 9th Military Naval Sector in Boka actually was?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about the build-up of that unit, no. To me it was part of the JNA military and here, navy. But the details of how the organisation was, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know who the commander of the 9th Military Naval Sector in Boka was?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not informed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who the commander of the Military Naval District in Split was?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were informed, to my great surprise, that it was Major General Mladenic, who was the commander in Lora base in Split, and he was the highest military authority we had contacted in Split, from the beginning to the end I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In tab 15 there is a letter addressed to General Kadijevic. Is it true that you never received an answer from him?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Say again, tab 15. Well, this letter is from the head of mission. And the answer should be to the head of mission. I haven't got.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look at what this letter is about, we can see that all of this is happening on the 10th of November. Is it you that the head of mission got the information from, that you sent Strugar, the commander of the JNA forces in the Dubrovnik area, a letter without receiving an answer from him? Were you the one who told the head of mission that -- the head of mission in Zagreb, did he receive this information from you?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: The head of mission in Zagreb received this message from me. I relayed the messages concerning Dubrovnik, or we did as such as a staff, to the head of mission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you not then inform the head of mission that the message to General Strugar was actually relayed to General Mladenic in Split because of the communication problems in relation to Dubrovnik and Boka?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we did that, too, but that I have no proof of. But that would be normal, that we passed and I'm -- and that the messages, as you have seen, sent to the complaints or protests, copies of that were also Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. forwarded to headquarters in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let us please move on to tab 17. On page 1 at the bottom of the letter, just next to the signature, there are two remarks or notes. Can you please read out what the last one says. It says: "It is not possible" -- can you please just read out the last two words, because I'm not sure I understand those.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neither am I, as half of it has been cut away. It says: "Not possible to have" -- but what was written before at the time I cannot read today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The letter is addressed to General Strugar, commander at the JNA at Boka Kotorska. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have information that General Strugar, as commander, was actually stationed in Boka?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was one of the informations I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we please briefly look at tab 40. There is a list of names for the JNA: General Strugar, Admiral Jokic, Jeremic, Uljarevic, Svicevic, Hasanagic. Is it correct that it is only next to Jeremic's name that you have a phone number there?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where this phone number is physically located?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you could only get in touch with Jeremic possibly, if communications were established?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know there was a list of other fax and telephone numbers available in Dubrovnik and in the ops office. But where the numbers actually ended, the numbers as such, I cannot remember. But we had -- we had lists of various contact numbers in both places and I think -- and also in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you then provide another list?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why I did?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whose phone number is from that list you had -- I mean, the phone numbers of course?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the numbers of this list, I'm sure we had them on the, let's say, the more professional list. This is apparently -- I don't know even who wrote this, but this is a -- typical notes taken by some EC monitor in some place to be brought back and then properly typed and listed and put on the wall. That's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whoever wrote this list failed to add other phone numbers, if there were any other phone numbers, in relation to JNA members?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please open tab 22 now. Can you please look at item 6 in this document in relation to the 10th and 11th of November.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The title says the 10th and 11th of November.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at item 6 it says, among other things: "We have been informed that certain projectiles had hit the inside of the Old Town. We were not in a position to assess the damage because we could not leave our hotel (in a material sense and pursuant to our instructions)." Did you locate that portion of the text?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain this sentence, what this word "material" means and then what does it mean exactly, "pursuant to our instructions."

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't write it, so that would have to be an interpretation, if that is what is wanted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, please, I'm sure you can tell us something about these instructions, as I believe that the monitors in Dubrovnik were receiving instructions from higher up; in this case that was you.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. The instructions were not -- never to put an EC monitor's life at risk. So they could not -- during shelling and when there was a danger for that, move out, when there is a risk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. In the next sentence it says: "All 14 members of the European Community for the last two days before departure spent all of their time at the hotel." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you just tell me again where we are now, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the next sentence.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under item 6 in relation to the 10th of November, the very next sentence.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Mr. Ghidi has reported it, I'm sure it's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we now go back to item 5 of this report in relation to the 5th of November, we will see that there are two references, one in the middle of the text. There is the following sentence: "For the whole day we have been trying in vain to get in touch with the JNA." And the last sentence under the same item: "It is not possible to get in touch with the JNA command in Boka Kotorska." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not -- that's the last sentence, and now you're mentioning at page 6 then. Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct what I've just read out to you?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when Mr. Ghidi has written it, I'm sure it's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In tabs 10 and 11 we looked at letters dated the 9th of November. In tab 13, a letter dated the 10th of November. In tab 15, a letter dated the 10th of November again. In tab 17, we looked at a letter dated the 13th of November. All these in relation to a fact in connection with the problem of establishing communication with the JNA in the Dubrovnik area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is in the same period that you received from Dubrovnik reports from your mission. Your reaction is set out in these letters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, and we tried to forward the protest through the best means we had. And down there we had the possibility of protesting directly to the other side, which was done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's precisely what I want to say. You secured your link with the JNA through the Dubrovnik authorities, first of all?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we tried to use the naval base and tried to go through our headquarters in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which naval base do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: The naval base in Split, as we have talked about before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean first you always go to the naval base in Split and to Zagreb before you try to get in touch with JNA members in the Dubrovnik area. Is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not my answer. Of course we first tried -- or the people in Dubrovnik, whoever was there, did their utmost to get in contact with the JNA in the area. When that type of communication failed, we did as anyone would do in this situation: Try all other means available.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't think there is any essential difference between what I said and what you said. It is my submission that the monitors based in Dubrovnik set up their link with JNA representatives through the Dubrovnik authorities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: When their own means did not work, they had to try to use the best possible means available. And if -- for example, borrowing a phone or a fax machine from the involved party would be quite a normal thing to do, as you have to get the messages through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The messages to the monitors in Dubrovnik, were they forwarded through the Crisis Staff in Dubrovnik, I mean messages from the JNA to the monitors? Were those forwarded through -- via the Crisis Staff in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Messages from the JNA to the EC monitors in Dubrovnik were forwarded to the -- what have you, the Hotel Argentina. I believe they were -- I don't believe there was a phone. It was a fax. And it was only if there was no contact, I believe, that the JNA passed messages to the crisis committee to have them forwarded to the EC monitors. Normally we tried to keep close -- direct contact, and we borrowed other means when possible --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, I must interrupt you there. Please try to keep your answer as brief as possible. My question now is: In this tab containing 42 pieces of evidence, can you find a single shred of paper that will corroborate what you are saying now, that there is indeed a paper trail that you received anything at all, any message at all, from the JNA at the Argentina Hotel?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was at the Argentina Hotel, messages were received --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Hvalkof --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I would object, Your Honour. He asks questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He asked the witness questions and then he won't let the witness respond to the question he's answering. This is the second time in a row he's asked a question, the witness is directly responding to that question, and then he cuts him off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am doing my best to try to get the witness focused on specifically what I'm asking him. I'm wasting a lot of time because his answers are unduly comprehensive. My specific question was whether in these 42 tabs, which he has before him, there is a single piece of evidence, single sheet of paper to corroborate that the JNA had direct communication with the Argentina Hotel, which is where the monitors were based. That is my question, and it's a yes or no question. That's the kind of answer it requires. Whereas, the witness goes off: When I was at the Argentina Hotel, so again he's talking about himself. I'm asking about all these 42 tabs. Is there any evidence of that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This occasion is one, Mr. Weiner, where the question does appear to be capable of a yes or no answer, although other questions today and yesterday have not been of that character. I suspect in this case the answer, Mr. Hvalkof, is no. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm a little doubtful now, Your Honour. The question going on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The question is whether in the 42 documents that have been presented through you by the Prosecution there is any record of a JNA communication.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think no. I can't comment anymore -- the indication.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we please now look at tab 24. Page 0218309 in reference to the meeting in Zelenika on the 14th of November, 1991. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first portion of the document says: "We wish to say where we are." Is this a reference to the JNA, JNA representatives? Is it?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what this means, this mark, NB.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's Latin; "nota bene" means something to remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it should also refer in this particular case to the positions put forth by the JNA, since they requested that the ZNG leave both Dubrovnik and Srdj?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Among these remarks related to the JNA, there is also a remark that says: "You have abused the Old Town. You should lay down your weapons to avoid conflict and the army will not go into town." Is this also a conclusion that is there?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where is that? Sorry I'm confused where that remark is, the last thing you said --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I have no problem with him questioning on -- questioning the witness on that. What he has just done, though, read line from -- read a passage from line 6 and then went down four more lines after another subject is discussed and read another line to try and link those two matters together. He read an issue which is currently on line 6: "You have misused" -- "you have been misusing the old" -- looks like Old Town. And then they talk about exchange of prisoners. Three JNA and then return 23 ZNG. And then the next line says: "You should put down weapons in order to avoid conflict." And he's read those two together as if it's the same topic. I have no problem with the cross-examination, but that's misreading or misquoting this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weiner. You've got page 308, have you, Mr. Hvalkof?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I was looking at 309.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Page 308, and we're still in the top half of the page. That's some lines down from where you were earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, you might like to repeat your question, Mr. Rodic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I can read it here, Your Honour. So you are asking me if the JNA is making a conclusion? Because this remark refers to notes I have been scribbling down of remarks given by the JNA representatives at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All I wanted is a confirmation. There are six or seven remarks in reference to observations made by the representatives of the JNA that you wrote down. I just wish to ask you additionally about two or three of those observations. I believe my learned friend from the OTP got it wrong. I wasn't trying to conceal anything from you by reading selectively from the document, as they have done in relation to the letters. It's all about these seven nota bene remarks that you wrote down, three of which I asked you specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I can see potential confusion here, Mr. Rodic. Perhaps it can be clarified by the witness. The points following your marginal note nota bene, are they comments that you have made, or are they notes of things said by the JNA representative?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are notes, my notes, conclusion of sort of -- as far as I remember it now when I look at it, of what was -- what they wanted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So you are seeking in note form to reproduce what was put to you by the JNA representative. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I was trying to put in a more clear handwriting than my nasty scribble here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Rodic, your question was on a different understanding. You thought these were the expressions of Mr. Hvalkof's view. If I have not been helpful, carry on then.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this page is very clear. Mr. Hvalkof noted down the messages he was receiving at that meeting from the representatives of the JNA. Then there is a line separating off those messages that came from the representatives of the Dubrovnik Crisis Staff. That is how the notes were kept. I only asked him from this first part the messages he noted down as having come from the representatives of the JNA, whether it is correct that the representatives of the JNA were pointing out that the Old Town was being misused, as noted down by Mr. Hvalkof, that arms should be laid down so as to avoid a conflict, and also that they said that the army would not enter the town. I think I have not concealed anything from him, because he can see all the notes on the page. What I am interested in is for him to confirm that the things I read out are correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this meeting, did the Crisis Staff tell you that they wanted a stable cease-fire? You can see that underneath this line.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we can all see it when -- it states the first line from the CC -- well, it's to me --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hvalkof, I'm just asking you for confirmation.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please turn to page 2. This top part of the page also relates to all the messages you heard from the JNA representatives, and you noted down their requests, just as on the previous page. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there mention here of the fact that the JNA wanted people from both sides to be at the observation posts, and you wrote down they wanted JNA plus monitors, "they," being the ZNG plus monitors. Does this mean that the JNA wanted the monitors on their side?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under the headline "Crisis Staff," did you hear from the representatives of the Crisis Staff that they were willing to accept demilitarisation under international control?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now please look at tab 27. Can you tell me Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. now in the upper left-hand corner it says: "Sent by the chief of the mission. Received by DAV." Can you explain this abbreviation?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person to whom this letter was addressed?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why are you so sure all of a sudden, because you know and you don't want to say or...

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: This abbreviation, to me it's not a name, it's an abbreviation. I have been asked about this before, and I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look -- if you look at paragraph 2, there is a sentence here: "The JNA proposal that would be locally discussed on the 25th of November was called an ultimatum by the Croatian side." Did you find this -- have you found it?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Dubrovnik had never in its history surrendered and would not do so now." This is followed by this sentence: "The Croatian government had issued strict instructions to the local authorities of Dubrovnik not to surrender their weapons." Is this contrary to what the Crisis Staff said on the issue of the demilitarisation of Dubrovnik at the meeting of the 14th of November?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no weapons about that. It's -- the letter is not written by me. I don't know who is it sent to. I think it's even what I -- that I should answer it. To me, it's a sort of more political question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hvalkof, as you have taken a solemn declaration, I think it would be proper for you to answer my question. In view of the fact that in most cases here you answered questions by the Prosecutor about questions that you personally did not draw up, documents compiled by other people during a period of time when you were not present at the place where they were drawing up the documents. Am I right in saying this?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you assist me by saying whether this standpoint of the Croatian government put forward by the head of mission in this letter differs from the position of the Crisis Staff of the 14th of November, some ten days previously, which you noted down because you had heard it from them?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It differs, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me whether through the reports of your monitors in Dubrovnik you received information to the effect that there was a conflict between the Croatian government and the Dubrovnik Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at tab 28 now. This is the memorandum of agreement, and would you please look at the introduction to this document where it says that: "On Monday, the 25th of November in Dubrovnik," and I underline the following. "The military and naval commanders of the JNA in the Dubrovnik area, General Damjanovic and Admiral Jokic on the JNA side," who was the military commander and who was the naval commander?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case it's mentioned General Damjanovic and Admiral Jokic. I say again, in this case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether it's correct that the persons on the other side were the mayor of Dubrovnik, Mr. Pero Poljanic and the commander of the Croatian National Army in the Dubrovnik area, Nikola Obuljen on the Croatian side. All this in the presence of Minister Kouchner. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what is written, so it must be correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It has not entered the transcript that Nikola Obuljen, the commander of the Croatian army in the Dubrovnik area, was also present at the meeting, as stated in this document. Is this correct? So on the Dubrovnik side, the meeting was attended by Nikola Obuljen and Pero Poljanic. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it states that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at item 2. Item 2 refers to promises by the local commanders and the local authorities who provided guarantees concerning the security of monitors. And it states that: "Under no circumstances are they or the locations where they are staying or operating to be fired upon or otherwise threatened." It's an important part of this agreement, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether among the signatures on this agreement you also see the signature of the commander of the Croatian army in the Dubrovnik area, that is Nikola Obuljen?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this mean that he did not undertake an obligation? He was an active participant at the meeting and yet he did not undertake the obligations mentioned in this memorandum.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to the questions put by the Prosecutor, you said that this document has no value because the JNA on the 5th or, that is, the 6th of December shelled the Dubrovnik area. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you now whether you say that up to the 5th and 6th of December the Croats did not fire at all from Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I didn't observe it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear about it, Mr. Hvalkof? There are many things that you did not see, yet you talked about them.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking about the 5th and 6th of December. On the 5th, we're having a meeting in Cavtat, no shooting. On the 6th, shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You misunderstand me, obviously. The document before you was signed on the 25th of November, ten days before the 6th of December. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told the Prosecutor during the examination-in-chief that this piece of paper was worthless, that it had no value, because the JNA on the 6th of December fired shells. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you: In these ten days preceding the 6th of December, did you hear or receive any information from your monitors or any protests from the JNA saying that the Croats had opened fire from Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no monitors in Dubrovnik until I came down on the 5th. They were evacuated earlier in November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive anything from JNA representatives informing you that the Croats had opened fire from Dubrovnik in this period?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge -- sorry, I say again. In them -- in Split during that -- there may be something in the files. I believe you are talking about what -- reports we received from JNA in Split from the observers evacuated until I came down on the 4th. That is most likely there had been complaints about firing. I cannot remember it, I am not aware of it, I cannot confirm, but it is likely, the conflict you had going on all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, because the Croatian commander did not sign this memorandum of agreement.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I add a word here. When it was questioned, military matters in Dubrovnik, we discussed with -- what we considered were civilian crisis committee members. And if he has been a member or not -- so it was normal civilian people in charge of the military the way we understood it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At meetings with the Crisis Staff of Dubrovnik, did you see among others Nikola Obuljen?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember these people's names. If you show me their faces, it may be possible. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at tab number 29.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a letter written by you personally, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a report, yes, to my headquarters in Split.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In item 2 of this report, is it correct that nothing was noted down at that meeting or that any decision was reached and that a new meeting was to be held on the 6th of December with no mention of any kind of signing of any agreements. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In item 3, if you can read through, just skim through A, B, C, and D, the conditions that were discussed. Did you hear proposals to this effect from the JNA even before the 5th of December?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hvalkof. Would you please read item 4 and tell me now, bearing in mind that you are using notes from the meeting, that is your report, is it correct that at the time you thought it was not possible to give a reasonable prediction as to what the final agreement, should there be one, would look like.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, previous experience told me so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this reflect your pessimistic views, in comparison to the optimistic views of the Croatian representatives?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not pessimistic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Would you now look at tab 30. During the examination-in-chief you said that you had spent the previous night, between the 5th and 6th of December and the early morning of the 6th of December up to 6.00, without hearing any kind of firing on the Dubrovnik area, and that none of your colleagues had heard this either. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at tab 42, the English page is 03053553.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you say the last numbers again. 55 --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 553. Would you please look at paragraph 2, the second part of the text which says: "At 0605 hours on the 6th of December, I woke up to the familiar sound" -- have you found this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this paragraph the fourth or fifth sentence says: Occasionally you would sleep well during the night and not hear anything. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have heard anything on that night then and testify to this with certainty? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sure all the other times I have been shelled I have heard it, and besides that, my colleagues would have woken me up if I had not heard it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Evidence that you slept well, Mr. Hvalkof, is the note in your diary that the shelling began at 6.00. In your statement to the Tribunal investigators you say it's about 5.45 that you heard shells being fired on Dubrovnik. And in your article, you say that at 6.05 you were awakened by the sound of shells. In the same article you say that the hotel guests told you that the shelling began at 5.35. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Military precision and correct information seems not to be your strong point as an ECMM monitor it appears.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for that remark. I woke up --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with it?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree then that these facts that I have read out indicate imprecision?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave the times, what occurred to me, what I heard, I gave the times other people gave me. And there's nothing unprecise in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's imprecise if you say that you heard fire at 5.45, because it's not true. Can we agree about that?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I have said I heard fire at 5.45, it is wrong, I have made a mistake, I apologise for it. I would -- it was reported to me by somebody down -- that they had heard fire that early.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I started this set of questions in connection with the 6th of December, and I would like to round off the 6th of December in a continuous set of questions. Is it a convenient time now or may I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there was a -- I just want to make a correction for the record, too. If -- counsel just again made a misquotation or made a misleading statement. We have the actual statement here of the witness, his statement to the OTP. It says: "On December 6th at approximately 5.45." It doesn't say at 5.45 something happened, approximately. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're wanting us to accept that 6.05 is approximately 5.45 or are you merely softening the difference, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm softening the difference. There's a difference between saying that you indicated at 5.45 and saying that approximately --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: All right. I'm sure Mr. Rodic would be well ready to accept that distinction. We will break now and --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the witness and to the Prosecutor. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hvalkof, in addition to the impositions we discussed before the break in relation to the start of the shelling, is it correct that in your journal, I am referring to tab 30, the section of the journal referring to the 6th of December, you failed to write down that at 14 minutes past 7.00 you sent a strong protest to Admiral Jokic?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier you made a marginal remark that you had made a call to Split and Zagreb, the regional centre. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it then be a justified move to doubt the precision of all the other information contained in the journal, such as, for example, the number of shells?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your submission that you are certain, based on your notes, that you had counted the exact number of shells per minute?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: My colleagues and I tried, and mostly they were doing that part of the job. And that was what we -- what I noted down. There was a lot of noise, I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this counting, this accurate counting, was not then done by you?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the time not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who counted the shells then and who relayed this information to you?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had two colleagues along with me, and they reported, say, now it's this and so on and now it's that, and so many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which of the two colleagues by name, if you can say, please, was the one who informed you?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to recall both of them. I say again, both of them, you want names? Right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Van de Beek and Brolund.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they both counting or just one of them? I want to know which one, if so.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were both counting, not at the same time, because one of them might be occupied by trying to pass messages, assist me in other ways, and the other one could be out observing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what their location was as they counted the shells in.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Outside at the -- there's a terrace outside Hotel Dubrovnik or several terraces down towards the sea. And from up there we have a pretty good view of the Old Town of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they not in shelters, your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they spend the whole time outside on the terrace in front of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No -- sorry, no. You could also stand -- in the room where we were, you could stand and observe from the window where you had a better observation from outside and when situations seemed not so pleasant, they would move just inside the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hvalkof, for example, in your journal you state that at 20 past 7.00, two shells fell on the Old Town. In your article under tab 42 you say at 7.40 the first shell fell -- the first shells fell on the Old Town. How do you explain this discrepancy? Again, there is a degree of imprecision involved, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was my paper written at the time. The article is not written to give a precise description. It is written without these papers, and it is not meant as a document as description of a situation to people who were interested and had asked me to write it. And I accept and agree, there is a difference of -- what is it? 20 minutes or something, yes. But what I wrote down here in this log sheet, as I call it, that was the facts what I noted down at the time, looking at my watch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is a fact, isn't it, that when you gave your statement to the investigators of the Tribunal and when you wrote your article, you used notes and documents, just like you do now, during your testimony?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used some notes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Despite the fact that you keep using your notes, there is discrepancy in terms of the information you provide, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference in timing, yes, I agree. And I didn't take it that serious of those -- I have not checked properly, but this document, my log sheet, states what happened while I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The accurate times that you gave in your article, were those recorded based on your memory of events, or were you also consulting your notes while writing the article?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was consulting notes available to me at the time and the memory, and this was not a long time after the incident. What I had exactly available in front of me I cannot comment on today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us where you were on the 6th of December when you were taking notes. Where did you spend the most time on that day?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Down at the basement at the Hotel Argentina in a room from where you could from the windows see the Old Town of Dubrovnik and with these terraces outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that you spent most of the time in the cellar?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is corroborated by your note, or rather, in your answer to a question by the Prosecutor in relation to the time being given as minutes past 11.00, where you stated that Minister Rudolf, too, was in the cellar of the Argentina Hotel in the same room as you and that the minister made a phone call to Zagreb. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were present there, yes. He made many calls -- tried to anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can you tell us, please, from the window -- could you observe anything at all from the cellar?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not a cellar; it was a room where hotel guests could stay and be. It was down in the bottom of the hotel, and yes, you could see the Old Town of Dubrovnik from the windows of that room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see the entire Old Town?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a slight corner from the room you could not see from the room, and that's one of the reasons why we walked outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see Srdj?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from that room, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a man who has spent a large portion of his life in the military, as a man who has a lot of experience with mortars, is it not to say the least unconvincing when you tell us that you heard no shells, no mortar shells, being fired from Dubrovnik itself?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear it, I did not observe it, and none of us did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see the section of the town that is just behind the Old Town facing Lovrijenac from where you were?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall the name Lovrijenac, so that's difficult to answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you pay any attention to the northern section of the Old Town, the portion of the Old Town facing Srdj, or rather, between the Old Town itself and Mount Srdj? Could you see that section of the town through your window?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from the window, to the best of my knowledge. There was a -- there was a corner to the right, which would indicate to me what you say the northern side. There was a portion of the Old Town or the walls there we could not see from the window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When my learned friend from the OTP asked you in relation to the time frame between 10.45 and 1100 hours in relation to the information that 15 {Realtime transcript read in error "50"] shells per minute were falling with several-minute intervals between them. About these 15 shells per minute, can you corroborate this for me on personal experience or is this something someone else told you at the time?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can remember a lot of impacts per minute. If you ask me today if I am absolutely sure I can remember 15 myself, not precisely, but it was quite a lot. I don't think 15 to the best of my knowledge as much is wrong. And it was basically reported by my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I interrupt, Mr. Rodic, just to note that the transcript seems to have recorded your last question as saying 5-0 shells per minute. I'm sure you said 1-5, 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's probably misinterpretation, Your Honour. I did say 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, it's been noted now and I'm sure it will be corrected in due course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what this means, the first words, in your entry at 1130 hours. They are not in English. "Zagreb," and then I presume something in Danish, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are quite right. I was tired, I wrote in Danish. It says: "Zagreb works, full speed," meaning that we had called -- informed Zagreb about the situation, so they were doing their best to try from their side to establish a cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How then do you explain this here at 1130 hours or 1139? You say: "At least two shells were fired in the direction of the Old Town." How could you know that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: How --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In the English language version, Mr. Rodic, it reads: "At least two impacts in direction of Old Town," not that two shells were fired in direction of Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honour. It must be the B/C/S translation that I'm using, so it may be a mistake on my part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on, please. At 11.41, can you please read what it says there.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: "One more big bang, same direction, not observed," which means -- when it says "not observed," at this time, somebody has been busy doing something else and we just heard the bang from the same direction or the explosion. And it's clearly stated "not observed," but direction is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are in the basement of the hotel. How is it possible for you to say from where you are what the direction of the shell is and where it is headed for?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It didn't say where it was headed for; it says "same direction." We had heard the sound coming in all the time and in general it is possible for people to say which direction. The sound came from the same direction as all the previous shelling observed. And it's clearly stated that this was not observed, but to the best of our knowledge and experience, it came from the same direction as the previous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you used the sound of the shell to tell the direction where the shell is coming from, but the sound can only come from the window of the room in which you are. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it sounded exactly like all the previous shells -- observed shelling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let us get this clear. You could only hear the sound of a shell through the window of the room in which you are, which means that the sound is coming from a totally different direction. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say "this unobserved explosion seemed to come from the same direction as the previous impact" or -- and that is all I say. And for -- I know that when I put down at that time "not observed" it's because it was not observed. And when those -- the others were observed where I have not put it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that moment, were you or another monitor perhaps standing next to a piano?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I wouldn't know. But I would not think so. Of course I can't remember who was standing next to a piano at any time. No, I would not know. I was certainly not, I can tell you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this a piano in the same room in which you were staying?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember if anyone was playing the piano in that room? Was anyone playing music or dancing?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Someone was playing the piano sometimes during the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't think that the sound of the piano would possibly interfere with counting the exact number of the shells falling, do you?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. If you had been there, you would realise that the sound was quite high. And as I said, most observations were made from the outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the marks you made in your journal, 11.44, 11.45, 11.46, two shells, one shell, two shells. Is it correct that if we look at this journal we can't really say which direction the shells came from, where they fell, or who was firing the shells?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. At the time, I sort of tried to cut down writing. All impacts referred to here are in the Old City.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that there is no entry in your diary specifying that the shells you are writing about are only the shells falling on the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, it's not mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 11.53, we have the following statement: "Barrage of fire from heavy machine guns." Can you tell me exactly where you heard the sound of these machine guns coming from.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard the sound, and it is, in my opinion, most likely - I cannot prove it and none of us could prove anything - it's most likely that it might have been a Croatian weapon. I have no clue where it came. The sound was there all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further you say: "Sporadic fire from different directions."

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which sort of fire are you talking about there? Are we talking about artillery fire, about rifle fire?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- the sporadic fire was -- as far as I remember it here now, small arms fire, nothing we could observe -- well, sporadic fire, HMD, heavy machine gun, machine gun, that sort of stuff. But we couldn't see where it came from. We could hear the noise, and for sure it was not from the seaside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At 11.58 you write: "20-millimetre canon fire." Therefore this is 20-millimetre gun or canon fire. Where does that come from?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also from unobserved direction, so I can't confirm where it came from. And I can remember that I heard myself, that sound, and I -- it was -- I -- one of my colleagues, who it was I can't remember, reported it also; heard, not observed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say you remember hearing this sound I assume. Is it true then, since we are talking about a 20-millimetre gun, that you were able to recognise it specifically? It must be much easier for you no doubt to distinguish that sort of fire if it's nearer to you rather than further off from you?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I don't know where it came from. You're right, the closer, the better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At 12.03 you say: "Machine gun fire near the hotel from the Croatian side."

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So here you have clearly identified fire is coming from the Croatian side by a machine gun.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me: How close to the hotel was that, exactly if you remember?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot. But I know that the reason why the Croatian side is mentioned is that one of the other - my colleagues - was out sort of trying to observe on the land side of the hotel. And that's why we are not spending much time out there because it was not pleasant at all. But that's why we tried now and then when it was reasonable to go and observe and we know that to the best of our knowledge that it was Croatian fire at that time because one of the people were out there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this mean that it was only this one occasion, at least as far as this is reflected in your journal, that this monitor came out of the hotel and stood at a place from which he could actually observe Mount Srdj?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not the only time, but that time was not very pleasant. We had shells landing at the corner of the hotel, which I have also mentioned someplace, at that site. So as I mentioned before, we are told that we are not sent out to get killed, so you were not moving out that side because a lot of nonsense was going on there. So it was now and then and it might have been out the door, it might have been through windows. I cannot tell you that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that since 11.39, or rather, 11.41 to the end of your journal you never make a single reference to any other shells falling on the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I talk about something about or report artillery fire in -- and that means that the shells were landing in the town, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was quite specific, and it refers to the Old Town. Is it true that as of that time you never mention any other shells falling on the Old Town, no reference in your journal. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At 1430 in the notes it says, among other things: "Admiral Jokic said he had to be in Belgrade at 1400 hours and suggests a meeting tomorrow at 12.00." Did Admiral Jokic mention that General Strugar was also going to Belgrade at the same time?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure of this?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally contact Jokic?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't contact him. We got this letter from the admiral we had negotiated with the day before in letter or fax message.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the entry for 1610 in your log. "Minister Rudolf informs me that General Strugar has now ordered immediate cease-fire." Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Responding to the Prosecutor's question about this entry during your examination-in-chief you said that Minister Rudolf contacted the JNA and that he told you that Strugar was back on the ground and that there would be a cease-fire. Do you remember what this expression "back on the ground" means? Does this mean he had been absent from the ground?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not know. It does not mean that I knew anything about that. It just suddenly appears that we have been talking to Admiral Jokic the day before, having a meeting with him, and General Strugar had not appeared. So now General Strugar suddenly appears on the scene again, and that's what I mean, now he's back on the ground -- sorry, I am not using my own language, but that's what I meant by it. We suddenly hear -- this time we had not heard really from General Strugar; now we hear from him again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at tab 31. Please look at tab 32 also, just the content of these messages.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these notes of protest addressed to Admiral Jokic in the VPS Boka?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In tab 31 you sent this directly to Admiral Jokic at the VPS Boka address. And yet today during your examination, you did not know what VPS Boka meant.

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I -- I can't remember that abbreviation. It's right what I said before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't know what Admiral Jokic's appointment was either, and yet you put down VPS Boka. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the information I had when -- that that was a correct address.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In tab 32, line 4, is there mention of the position from which fire was opened? There is a list of tank, mortar, and boat artillery fire on Dubrovnik. This is from the letter of the Crisis Staff. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This piece of information corresponds with what is in your logbook of the 6th of December at 6.00 when you say: "Shelling began from land and sea towards the fortress near Srdj and the harbour." Were you able to observe firing from the sea at that time?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was fire from the sea. Not much, but it was there. The exact time, it should be in the logbook.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was firing?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: We observed some navy units, and I had no knowledge about what type of units there were. They didn't seem to be that big to me, but there were navy units observed. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they looked like normal navy units, grey-coloured, and that's -- and they were firing in the direction of Dubrovnik, as far as I remember now. But that's what they do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say what army these units belonged to?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they could have belonged to the Croatian army or to the JNA, the navy. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at tab 33. This is a letter from Minister Rudolf addressed to General Strugar to -- at VPS Boka. Have you found the document?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 3 of this document it states that: "Minister Rudolf arrived in Dubrovnik and Cavtat with two other members of the government of Croatia because he had received a guarantee from the supreme command of the armed forces of the SFRY and the command of the VPO Split that he would be able to arrive safely for negotiations with the representatives of the JNA in Cavtat." Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the line correct then, the military naval sector Boka; the Military District of Split, as the next level; and then the highest level, the supreme command of the armed forces of the SFRY. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what's written here, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this letter, in the paragraph before the last, Minister Rudolf informs General Strugar that the Federal Secretary for National Defence, General Kadijevic, has ordered an investigation to establish an irresponsibility of the members of the JNA for the suffering inflicted on Dubrovnik. And the last sentence of this paragraph says: "I am convinced that this investigation will be correct and you will certainly find what the results are." This was written by Minister Rudolf to General Strugar. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that Minister Rudolf does not say who is to conduct the investigation on the ground? Is it correct that he does not mention who will carry out the investigation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it is. No person is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Minister Rudolf then is informing General Strugar that an investigation will be carried out on the basis of what he heard from Kadijevic. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what is written here is what the minister read -- wrote, so it must be correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's correct then that according to this letter General Strugar will be informed of the results of the investigation. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER HVALKOF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
